Hi! 
I'm trying to run a simple "iid" model and I obtain the following error:
GMRFLib version 3.0-0-snapshot, has recived error no [12]
Reason    : The Newton-Raphson optimizer did not converge
Message   : Condition `lambda < 1.0 / lambda_lim' is not TRUE
Function  : GMRFLib_init_GMRF_approximation_store__intern
File      : approx-inference.c
Line      : 2701
RCSId     : file: approx-inference.c  hgid: eac68d10cc0f  date: Mon Feb 10 14:18:28 2014 +0100

/bin/sh: line 1:   701 Abort trap: 6           '/Users/cokerer/Library/R/3.0/library/INLA/bin/mac/64bit/inla' -b -s -v '/var/folders/zz/zyxvpxvq6csfxvn_n0004rkm00164n/T//Rtmpb2SY3A/file12b659a6b63/Model.ini' > /var/folders/zz/zyxvpxvq6csfxvn_n0004rkm00164n/T//Rtmpb2SY3A/file12b659a6b63/Logfile.txt
Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() : 
  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.

Here is my code:
formula = bw ~ 1+no2+p.black+p.edu+p.pov+pc+inc+f(cnty, model="iid")
result = inla(formula, family="gaussian", data=data.tract)

Its not clear to me what is going on here. 

Thanks,
Eric

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Error: GMRFLib version 3.0-0-snapshot, has recived error no [12]
parts:
On Wed, 2014-02-19 at 18:24 -0800, Eric Coker wrote:
> Thank you, that seems to have been the issue. The other question I
> have is with regard to dataset size. I have 1.5 million observations
> and I wish to run a model with 2,261 census tracts for the random
> effects grouping variable. Have you run into upper limits regarding
> dataset sizes, particularly with sizes that I have just described.

Hi

due to the way its implemented, we create a graph with one node for each
observation, hence the graph-size depends (internally) also on the
number of observation + the size of the model itself. this might be an
issue with your example, as 1.5E6 is a large number... depending on the
structure of the model, usually around 500E3 - 1000E3 seems to run fine,
yours is a bit larger, but it is so dependent on the structure of the
model so its impossible to give general rules.

so you can try to increase the size of the model/data until it does not
run smooth anymore. there are strategies for which you can use to make
it run a bit more, like reducing the number of threads use to reduce the
memory use, avoid integrating out the hyperparameter will also reduce
the memory use, etc. A larger computational server will be usefull here
I guess.

Best
H


--
Håvard Rue
he...@r-inla.org
